item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Jo has three metal blocks. The weight of each block is the same.
When she weighed one block against 8 grams, this is what happened.

[Image: The block is lighter than the weight of 8 grams on the scale.]

When she weighed all three blocks against 20 grams, this is what happened.

[Image: The three blocks are heavier than the weight of 20 grams on the scale.]

Which of the following could be the weight of one metal block?
item.figure_description:
Two balance scale diagrams:
- Top balance scale: The beam is tilted down to the right. On the higher left pan rests one gray rectangular metal block. On the lower right pan rest four weights: one large weight labeled "5g" and three small weights stacked beside it, each labeled "1g" (total 8 grams).
- Bottom balance scale: The beam is tilted down to the left. On the lower left pan rests a stack of three identical gray rectangular metal blocks. On the higher right pan rest two large weights, each labeled "10g" (total 20 grams).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The objects on the scale make it balance exactly. On the left pan there is a 1 kg weight (mass) and half a brick. On the right pan there is one brick.

[Image: A balance scale with objects on each pan]

What is the weight (mass) of one brick?
reference_items.figure_description: A two-pan balance scale is shown balanced horizontally on a central pivot and base. On the left pan, there is a weight labeled "1 kg" shaped like a standard counterweight, and a standing rectangular block representing half a brick. On the right pan, there is a larger rectangular block representing one whole brick, which has the same height as the block on the left pan but twice its width.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

Four stacks of identical cubic blocks shown in perspective:
- Option A: A stack of blocks 2 cubes wide, 2 cubes deep, and 2 cubes high.
- Option B: A flat stack of blocks 3 cubes wide, 4 cubes deep, and 1 cube high.
- Option C: A stack of blocks 6 cubes wide, 1 cube deep, and 2 cubes high.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A rectangular prism, with a length of 5 blocks, width of 4 blocks, and height of 3 blocks. There is a hole shown on the top of the rectangular prism. The hole is 2 blocks by 3 blocks and goes all the way through the shape.]

The figure above shows a shape made up of cubes that are all the same size. There is a hole all the way through the shape. How many cubes would be needed to fill the hole?
reference_items.figure_description: An isometric drawing of a 3D block shape constructed from identical unit cubes. The overall block is 5 cubes wide along the front, 4 cubes deep along the right side, and 3 cubes tall. In the center of the top face, there is a rectangular rectangular hole measuring 3 cubes wide by 2 cubes deep, bordered by a rim that is 1 cube wide on all four sides. The hole extends vertically straight down through the entire height of 3 cubes.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
ABCD is a trapezoid.

[Image: Trapezoid ABCD]

Another trapezoid, GHIJ (not shown), is congruent (the same size and shape) to ABCD. Angles G and J each measure 70°. Which of these could be true?

options.label: B
options.text: Angle H is a right angle.

options.label: C
options.text: All sides of GHIJ are the same length.

options.label: D
options.text: The perimeter of GHIJ is 3 times the perimeter of ABCD.

options.label: E
options.text: The area of GHIJ is less than the area of ABCD.

reference_items.figure_description: An isosceles trapezoid ABCD with horizontal base AD along the bottom and shorter horizontal side BC along the top. Vertex A is at the bottom left, B is at the top left, C is at the top right, and D is at the bottom right. The interior angle at vertex A is labeled 70°, and the interior angle at vertex D is labeled 70°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis from 26 to 28. There are four marks in between 26 to 27, as well as in between 27 to 28. K is marked underneath the last mark between 27 and 28.]

Which number does K represent on this number line?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal number line with arrowheads at both ends. There are evenly spaced vertical tick marks. The first labeled tick mark is labeled 26 below the line. Between 26 and 27, there are 4 evenly spaced tick marks dividing the interval into 5 equal parts. The tick mark for 27 is labeled below the line. Between 27 and 28, there are 4 evenly spaced tick marks, with the fourth tick mark labeled with the letter K below the line. The next tick mark is labeled 28 below the line. The line extends slightly past 26 to the left and past 28 to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A ruler with a wavy string above it]

If the string in the diagram is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description: A metric ruler marked from 0 to 11 cm, with ticks at every centimeter and half-centimeter, labeled 'cm' at the left end and with numbers 1 through 11. Above the ruler, a curved line labeled 'string' begins at the 3 cm mark, extends horizontally to approximately 5.5 cm, loops back leftward to about 4.7 cm, and then extends horizontally rightward, ending near the 7 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this figure, PQ and RS are parallel.

[Image: Parallel lines PQ and RS intersected by a transversal]

Of the following, which pair of angles has the sum of 180°?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrowheads at both ends are intersected by a transversal line that slopes upward from lower-left to upper-right. The upper horizontal line has label P at its left end and Q at its right end. The lower horizontal line has label R at its left end and S at its right end. At the intersection with line PQ, four angles are numbered: angle 1 in the upper-left, angle 2 in the upper-right, angle 3 in the lower-right, and angle 4 in the lower-left. At the intersection with line RS, four angles are numbered: angle 5 in the upper-left, angle 6 in the upper-right, angle 7 in the lower-right, and angle 8 in the lower-left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
